title: Awaiting the primary record
context: A summary is available, but the first requested record has not yet been examined.
action: Request the original record and identify which part of the summary it is meant to support.
limit: Keep the conclusion pending; a summary alone cannot establish the source contents.

title: Referenced appendix absent
context: The supplied packet refers to an appendix that is not included among its attachments.
action: Request the named appendix and confirm that it belongs to the same document version.
limit: Do not infer that the absent appendix either supports or contradicts the summary.

title: Property reference differs
context: The summary and a supporting record identify different property references.
action: Ask the provider to reconcile the references before applying either record to the proposed property.
limit: A relevant-looking record for another property does not resolve this property's question.

title: Reporting windows differ
context: Two records cover different start or end dates, so the comparison is not aligned.
action: Request a bridge for the uncovered interval and retain both original periods.
limit: A difference caused by timing must not be silently described as a performance difference.

title: Superseded draft retained
context: A draft and a later revision are both in the packet, but neither is labeled as current.
action: Ask the responsible party which version is operative and what changed between them.
limit: The last file received is not automatically the operative version.

title: Verbal update only
context: A conversation reportedly changed a material detail, but no written update is in the packet.
action: Request a written confirmation from the appropriate party and retain the prior record.
limit: Your notes about a conversation do not amend a proposal or establish an external fact.

title: Unreadable attachment
context: A listed attachment cannot be read well enough to inspect its relevant fields.
action: Request a readable copy with the source identity, scope and dates intact.
limit: A file being present is different from its contents being reviewable.

title: Summary conflicts with source
context: A summary states that the question is resolved, while the retained source shows an open item.
action: Record the specific disagreement and request a reconciliation tied to the source item.
limit: Do not choose the more favorable statement merely because it is easier to use.

title: Duplicate filenames
context: Several files have the same name, but their contents or dates differ.
action: Assign stable source references and ask which copies are duplicates or revisions.
limit: A filename is not enough to establish document identity.

title: Observation date missing
context: The packet shows when a file was received but not when the underlying observation was made.
action: Ask for the observation date and distinguish it from issue and receipt dates.
limit: A recent upload does not establish that the underlying evidence is current.

title: Provider scope unavailable
context: A provider's conclusion is quoted without the scope of work under which it was prepared.
action: Request the scope, exclusions and relevant limitations before interpreting the conclusion.
limit: A conclusion cannot safely be extended beyond the work actually performed.

title: Acknowledgment not recorded
context: The packet includes a proposed handoff, but no record that the intended recipient acknowledged it.
action: Ask the recipient to identify what was received and what remains outstanding.
limit: Sending a file is not proof that it was accessible, examined or accepted.

title: Incomplete document pages
context: Only part of a multi-page record is available, and the missing pages may contain context.
action: Request the complete record, including attachments and page numbering where available.
limit: An excerpt should not be treated as the full record.

title: Definitions conflict
context: The summary and a source use the same label for different scopes or measures.
action: Write both definitions and ask for a comparison on a common basis.
limit: Matching words do not guarantee matching underlying meanings.

title: Responsible source unclear
context: A statement is circulated without identifying the person or organization responsible for it.
action: Request provenance and the source's role in the matter being reviewed.
limit: An unattributed statement cannot be assigned an invented author or authority.

title: Assumption presented as observation
context: A future estimate appears in the same presentation as observed information without a clear label.
action: Separate assumed, quoted and observed fields and request the basis of the estimate.
limit: A detailed estimate remains conditional rather than a recorded outcome.

title: Neighboring example substituted
context: An example from a different property is being used to answer a property-specific question.
action: Retain it as background and request the records needed for the actual property.
limit: An adjacent or similar property does not establish the same rights, condition or result.

title: Service stage differs
context: The available account concerns an earlier stage than the stage now being evaluated.
action: Record the actual stage covered and request evidence specific to the later stage.
limit: An early experience cannot establish an unobserved later outcome.

title: Condition remains outstanding
context: The source describes a conclusion that depends on a condition not shown as completed.
action: Identify the condition, its owner and the evidence needed to establish completion.
limit: Conditional language must remain attached to the conclusion.

title: Exclusion omitted from summary
context: The underlying record contains an exclusion absent from the summary.
action: Carry the exclusion into the comparison and request clarification of its effect.
limit: Removing a limitation can materially change the meaning of an otherwise accurate statement.

title: Source link inaccessible
context: A citation points to a record that the reviewer cannot access.
action: Request an authorized, readable copy or a working reference without copying private credentials.
limit: The existence of a link does not establish that its contents were reviewed.

title: Evidence needs refresh
context: The record predates a material change described elsewhere in the packet.
action: Ask which findings remain applicable and which require an updated observation.
limit: An old record should not be treated as current solely because it is the only one available.

title: Independent corroboration unavailable
context: The available sources all repeat one originating statement, and no separate corroboration is supplied.
action: Identify the original statement and describe the corroboration that has and has not been examined.
limit: Repeated publication of one claim is not multiple independent observations.

title: Third-party boundary unclear
context: A company summary describes work that may be performed under a separate third-party agreement.
action: Map the specific task to the actual provider and request the relevant scope.
limit: Do not infer that one firm's service description establishes another firm's obligations.

title: Task owner not assigned
context: The packet identifies an open question but assigns no party to obtain the answer.
action: Name a responsible party, a precise request and a follow-up date.
limit: A shared task list without an owner can leave the central question unresolved.

title: Time pressure before evidence
context: A target decision date is approaching while a material source remains pending.
action: Separate the target date from the evidence gate and record what remains unexamined.
limit: A short timeline does not convert missing information into an established fact.

title: Revision not propagated
context: A source was revised, but dependent summaries still show the old conclusion.
action: Trace the changed item through every affected summary and retain a revision trail.
limit: Updating one input without dependent outputs creates an inconsistent comparison.

title: Response without supporting record
context: A response says the issue was addressed but does not include the record needed to demonstrate it.
action: Request the specific completion evidence rather than treating the response as the evidence itself.
limit: A promise or assertion of completion is distinct from documented completion.

title: Selected excerpt only
context: The packet presents a selected excerpt without the surrounding context or selection rule.
action: Request sufficient context to determine what the excerpt actually establishes.
limit: A selected passage need not represent the full record or the full range of experiences.

title: Units not aligned
context: The relevant fields use different units or time bases, and no conversion is shown.
action: Write the units explicitly and show the conversion before comparing the values.
limit: A numerical comparison without aligned units can imply a difference that is not real.

title: Complete-packet claim overstated
context: The packet is labeled complete even though a required record is listed as missing.
action: Define completeness for this question and keep the absent item visible.
limit: A broad completeness label does not fill a specific evidence gap.

title: Repeated source counted twice
context: Two apparent supporting items are copies or summaries of the same underlying record.
action: Group them under one source reference and distinguish repetition from corroboration.
limit: The number of attachments is not the number of independent supporting observations.

title: Provenance not retained
context: The packet contains a copied statement with no stable reference back to its origin.
action: Request the original publisher, record date and precise location of the relevant material.
limit: Do not invent a source or treat a copied claim as authenticated evidence.

title: Figure detached from context
context: A number or label is supplied without the scope, period or definition that produced it.
action: Request the surrounding definition and supporting schedule before using the figure.
limit: A precise-looking value may still be unusable for the intended comparison.

title: Handoff has open exceptions
context: The handoff lists delivered material alongside unresolved exceptions without a follow-up owner.
action: Retain the exception list and assign responsibility for obtaining the missing evidence.
limit: A completed handoff does not necessarily mean every substantive question is resolved.

title: Cross-source exception unresolved
context: The packet contains two source positions that cannot both describe the same scope as presented.
action: Preserve both positions and request the smallest factual clarification needed to reconcile them.
limit: An unresolved discrepancy is a reason for a narrower conclusion, not an invented explanation.

title: Specialist boundary reached
context: The open question requires expertise beyond the scope of the general project coordinator.
action: Assign the question to the appropriate qualified party and request a scoped response.
limit: This workbook does not supply legal, technical, tax or other specialist approval.

title: Unpriced dependency
context: A necessary follow-up is identified, but its scope, cost or availability remains unconfirmed.
action: Request a scoped quote or availability statement and keep the dependency separate from confirmed work.
limit: An unpriced task is not a zero-cost task or a confirmed service commitment.

title: Readiness gate still open
context: The summary says the project is ready while a designated evidence gate is unresolved.
action: Compare the readiness definition with the actual open gate and record the decision basis.
limit: A broad readiness status does not override a specific unresolved prerequisite.

title: All listed records reviewed
context: Every listed source is marked examined for this training packet, with no stated mismatch remaining.
action: Write the narrow conclusion supported by those records and identify any matters outside their scope.
limit: Checklist completion is not independent authentication, certification or a guarantee of outcome.
